correction.text: Iberia (Kartli) under its presiding princes, Tbilisi as capital: 'Iberia became a Persian province ruled by a marzpan' until Maurice sent Guaram I in 588

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 588-681, which Cliopatria lacks (its first Principality shape is 682). The page names Kartli (Iberia) as the principality's core, with Tbilisi as capital; it gives no boundary and no area, so the region is the gazetteer's Kartli.

Cliopatria's 34,636 km2 shape sits on Kartli (bbox 42.5-45.7E, 41.1-43.1N). The page gives no area and no boundary, only Kartli as core, so the shape is accepted as the honest precision of the era; the page names a Chosroid revolt 'in the 680s' but no change of land.

Unchanged in extent (34,712 km2 against 34,636). 'In 724, al-Jarrah captured Tiflis and brought Caucasian Iberia and the lands of the Alans under Muslim suzerainty' (Arab-Khazar wars); the land stays drawn as the principality's, with the suzerainty carried by the Umayyad dossier.

Cliopatria draws one shape for 732-740, but Tbilisi was taken in 735/736: 'In that year, Marwan II took hold of Tbilisi and much of the neighbouring lands' (Emirate of Tbilisi: established 736). The shape holds for 732-735 only; from 736 use new keyframe principality-of-iberia_736. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 732..735 from this entry's own 'valid for 732-735 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Kartli without Tbilisi and its immediate lands, which passed to the Arab emir installed in 736

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 736-813: the Cliopatria shape without Tbilisi, where 'a Muslim emir was installed in the 730s' (Principality page); the seat moves to Uplistsikhe (c. 736-813). The 30 km radius is a reading ('much of the neighbouring lands' is not measured; the page adds that Muslim influence was 'strictly confined to the city itself'). Cliopatria draws nothing for Iberia after 740.

ledger.note: 588: Maurice sends Guaram I to rule Iberia. 'Maurice did respond, and, in 588, sent his protégé, Guaram I of the Guaramids, as a new ruler to Iberia'; the lead dates the principality to 'around 580', after the Sassanids 'seized on the opportunity to abolish the Iberian monarchy' on Bakur III's death in 580. The Byzantine-Sassanid treaty of 591 'confirmed this new rearrangement'.

627: Heraclius's intervention replaces the Guaramids with the pro-Byzantine Chosroids (Adarnase I, 627-637/642): 'Heraclius attacked Tbilisi in 626', Stephen I died, and Heraclius 'reinstated a member of the more pro-Byzantine Chosroid house'. Same state, same colour; the year 627 is the princes' table (Adarnase I 627-637/642), the page's own sentence gives 626.

724: al-Jarrah takes Tiflis. 'In 724, al-Jarrah captured Tiflis and brought Caucasian Iberia and the lands of the Alans under Muslim suzerainty'; the Emirate page adds that the Arabs first appeared in Kartli in 645 and that firm control came only in 735.
736: the princely seat leaves Tbilisi for Uplistsikhe (infobox: Tbilisi c. 588-736, Uplistsikhe c. 736-813).

region.text: Tbilisi and much of the neighbouring lands

ledger.note: 736: an Arab emir is installed at Tbilisi. 'In that year [735], Marwan II took hold of Tbilisi and much of the neighbouring lands'; infobox 'Established: 736'; the Principality page: the Arabs 'dispossessed them of Tbilisi where a Muslim emir was installed in the 730s'. The page text says 735, the infobox 736; the radius is a reading.

736: the fighting over Tbilisi ends with the emirate. The Marwan II campaign is dated c. 735-737 in the Arab-Khazar wars page, which has him push 'into Iberia' and drive its ruler to Anakopia in Abkhazia.

c. 748: the Nersianids replace the Guaramids for a generation. 'The Guaramids were briefly succeeded by the Nersianids between c. 748 and 779/80'; the Guaramids 'had vanished once and for all by 786'. Same state, same colour.
813: the princely seat moves to Artanuji (infobox: Artanuji c. 813-888), in Klarjeti; carried on by kingdom-of-the-iberians.

region.text: Kartli without Tbilisi (new keyframe 736), the land of the principality when the seat left

ledger.note: 813: the last Iberian prince leaves Kartli for Klarjeti. 'In 813, the last Iberian prince Ashot I of the Bagrationi dynasty established himself in his patrimonial Duchy of Klarjeti'; the Bagratid line continues as the Kingdom of the Iberians (Cliopatria 814-999, whose infobox calls 813-888 a principality and 888 the kingdom). Kartli itself falls to the Emirate of Tbilisi and local nobles; the page is silent on who held it in 814-887 (Bagrat I 'regained central Iberia' only briefly in 853).

wars.name: Arab-Khazar wars
wars.outcome: Al-Jarrah took Tiflis in 724 and brought Caucasian Iberia under Muslim suzerainty; Marwan ibn Muhammad pushed into Iberia in c. 736 and drove its ruler to Anakopia; an Arab emir held Tbilisi from 735/736 (Emirate of Tbilisi).
wars.note: The Emirate page dates the taking of Tbilisi to 735, its infobox to 736. The principality is a victim and a theatre rather than a principal belligerent.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or an area; Kartli is the core, the Tbilisi enclave from 736 is a radius reading.

notes:
Four pages were opened against a 1-2 page budget because the Emirate, Arab-Khazar and Kingdom pages are shared with the neighbouring dossiers (kingdom-of-the-iberians, kingdom-of-lazica).

START AND END. Cliopatria's Principality row is 682-740 only. The Principality page gives 'Established c. 588' (the lead says 'around 580') and runs the principality to 888. This dossier covers 588-813: the Kartli years with new keyframes for 588-681 and 736-813, ending in 813 when 'the last Iberian prince Ashot I ... established himself in his patrimonial Duchy of Klarjeti'. Cliopatria draws the Bagratid line of Klarjeti/Tao from 814 under Kingdom of the Iberians (814-999), and that page's infobox gives 'Principality (c. 813-888)' then 'Feudal Monarchy (888-1008)'. A reviewer who prefers the page's 888 should move the 814-887 shapes here; the cost is that the colour would then change in 888 for no change of land.

KARTLI 814-887: no page opened says who held Kartli outside Tbilisi; the Kingdom of the Iberians page has Bagrat I regaining central Iberia in 853 and the 880 seizure of the Tbilisi emir, and Cliopatria's Georgia row starts a large shape (86,640 km2, bbox 39.1-47.8E) in 888. The georgia dossier (eu-19) and the kingdom-of-the-iberians dossier should settle it.

SUZERAINTY. The Chosroids 'were forced to recognize the suzerainty of the Umayyad Caliph in the 640s' (page wording; the Emirate page has the Arabs in Kartli in 645), 'revolted, unsuccessfully, against the Arab hegemony in the 680s', and Iberia was brought under Muslim suzerainty in 724 (Arab-Khazar wars). The vassal_start events belong in the suzerain's dossier (umayyad-caliphate, abbasid-caliphate) with counterpart principality-of-iberia; none of the pages gives an end year other than 813.

MISSING DOSSIERS. emirate-of-tbilisi (736-1122) and principality-of-kakheti (the Chosroid line, named as successors in the infobox) need dossiers; the gazetteer has Tbilisi and Kakheti already.

UNVERIFIED. Rulers are not given: the page's princes table was only partly read. The 682 and 724 shapes are accepted as Kartli; the page gives neither area nor boundary.
